column3: Some of the following routines require that certain registers and/or
variables be set up with certain values before calling them.  If an
error is generated while in one of these routines, the normal error
message will be generated and the routine will return control to
BASIC.  In order to prevent this from happening, the error must be
intercepted by using the ram hook for the error processing routine

column5: DESCRIPTION
FIX NUMBER IN FPA0 - Converts the number in FPA0
to an integer value and forces it to be positive.
EVALUATE &H - Get the value after the &H from the
program line and convert it to a numerical value.
GET CALPOS ROUTINE ADDRESS - Get the address of
the routine which will convert the horizontal and
vertical coordinates into an absolute screen
address and pixel mask depending upon the current
PMODE. Return the address of the routine in the
U register.
CALPOS FOR CURRENT PMODE - This routine jumps to
the correct calpos routine depending upon the
current PMODE.
CALPOS 2 COLOR MODE - Calculates toe absolute
screen address and pixel mask for the 2 color hires
mode. Enter with X,Y coordinates in HORBEG and
VERBEG and exit with address in the X register and
the pixel mask in ACCA.
CALPOS 4 COLOR MODE - Calculates toe absolute
screen address and pixel mask for the 4 color hires
mode. Enter with X,Y coordinates in HORBEG and
VERBEG and exit with address in the X register and
the pixel mask in ACCA.
ADJUST SCREEN POINTER DOWN A ROW - Move the X
register down one graphic row.  The number of
bytes per horizontal graphic row must be in HORBYT.
MOVE A PIXEL TO THE RIGHT (2 COLOR) - Adjust the X
register and ACCA one pixel position to the right in
the 2 color mode.  Enter with the absolute screen
address in the X register and the pixel mask in ACCA.
MOVE A PIXEL TO THE RIGHT (4 COLOR) - Adjust the X
register and ACCA one pixel position to the right in
the 4 color mode.  Enter with the absolute screen
address in the X register and the pixel mask in ACCA.
NORMALIZE COORDINATES - Adjust the horizontal and
vertical coordinates for the current PMODE. Enter
with X,Y coordinates in HORBEG and VERBEG, the
normalized coordinates will be returned in the same.
TURN ON A PIXEL - Turn on the pixel which is
being pointed to by the X register (absolute
screen address) and ACCA (pixel mask) to the color
in ALLCOL. Set CHGFLG <> 0 if pixel color was
unchanged by the action.
DRAW A BOX - Encloses a diagonal line with a box
(box function of LINE). Enter with the start and
end coordinates of the original line in HORBEG,
VERBEG, HOREND and VEREND.
FILL BOX - Draw a series of horizontal lines
from BERBEG to VEREND
DRAW A HORIZONTAL LINE - Draw a horizontal line from
HOREND to HORBEG at the vertical coordinate VERBEG
with the color in ALLCOL.
DRAW A VERTICAL LINE - Draw a vertical line from
VEREND to VERBEG at the horizontal coordinate
HORBEG with the color in ALLCOL.
POINT TO PIXEL MOVE ROUTINE - Point the U register
to the routine which will move the current pixel
to the right one position for the current PMODE.
DRAW A LINE - Draw a line from (HORBEG,VERBEG) to
(HOREND, VEREND).
INCREMENT HORIZONTAL POSITION - Gets the current
horizontal coordinate (HORBEG) and moves it one
to the right.
INCREMENT VERTICAL POSITION - Gets the current
vertical coordinate (VERBEG) and moves it one down.
DECREMENT HORIZONTAL POSITION - Gets the current
horizontal coordinate (HORBEG) and moves it one
to the left.
DECREMENT VERTICAL POSITION - Gets the current
vertical coordinate (VERBEG) and moves it one up.
GET MAXIMUM COORDINATES - Get the maximum values
of the horizontal and vertical coordinates for the
current PMODE. Return HOR in VD3 and VER in VD5.
CLEAR GRAPHIC SCREEN - Clear the current graphics
screen to the color in ACCB.  If ACCB = 0 then
clear to the current background color.
CALCULATE ABS(VEREND-VERBEG) - Calculate the
absolute value of the distance between VEREND
and VERBEG. Carry flag will indicate which was
the larger coordinate.
CALCULATE ABS(HOREND-HORBEG) - Calculate the
absolute value of the distance between HOREND
and HORBEG. Carry flag will indicate which was
the larger coordinate.
16 BIT MULTIPLY - Multiply (unsigned) two 16 bit
numbers together.  Enter with one number in ACCD
and the other in the X register.  The four byte
product will be returned in the Y and U registers.
